html:
The Hän, or Hwëch'in, "people of the river", are an Athabaskan people of the upper Yukon River, on both sides of today's border between Alaska and Canada's Yukon. Their lands centred on the river around the mouth of the Klondike River and Eagle, Alaska.

They fished salmon at summer camps, hunted caribou and moose, and traded with their Gwich'in neighbours. In 1896 gold was found on a creek in their country, and the Klondike Gold Rush brought tens of thousands of miners. Dawson City grew up on their fishing camp at the Klondike mouth, and the Hän were moved a few kilometres downriver to Moosehide. Today they belong to the Tr'ondëk Hwëch'in First Nation in Dawson and the village of Eagle in Alaska.
